the development of automated signalized junction controllers that learn strategies from a trained human expert.
the application of machine learning techniques to the control of traffic junctions.
the development of a signal control system that is both adaptive and robust to variation in network topology and traffic demand.

the machine learning junction control strategy can outperform both High Bid and MOVAs in terms of average delay, and is more equitability in terms of variance of journey times.
the machine learning junction controller can be trained by a human to outperform both High Bid and MOVAs.

the machine learning junction control systems are able to outperform High Bid, MOVA and the human expert in terms of average delay, and outperform High Bid but not MOVA or the human expert in equitability, for the networks considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of a human expert to train machine learning junction controllers is effective.

machine learning techniques can provide an effective means for developing automated signal control strategies that are capable of learning from a human expert and that can outperform existing signal control systems.

machine learning junction controllers trained by human experts are capable of outperforming existing systems in terms of minimizing delay and maximizing equability, whilst being robust to variations in the positioning accuracy and the fraction of vehicles fitted with probes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance of machine learning junction control systems trained by human experts can be superior to that of systems that are hand-crafted by human experts, and that this is achieved with no prior knowledge of the network structure.
the use of machine learning techniques can be used to learn strategies from a domain expert and can outperform other control strategies in terms of average delay and equitability.
